title: Later Yan
capsule: Later Yan (384–409) was a Sixteen Kingdoms state founded by Murong Chui of the Xianbei Murong clan after he broke from Former Qin following the Battle of Fei River (383) and established his capital at Zhongshan in Hebei. Murong Chui reunified much of the old Former Yan realm by 394, defeating the rival Western Yan at Ye and controlling a vast arc from Hebei to Liaoning. His son Murong Bao's catastrophic defeat by Northern Wei at the Battle of Canhe Slope (395) halved the state and drove the court to Longcheng in Liaoning. Successive coups — Lan Han's usurpation (398), Murong Sheng's reconquest, and finally Murong Xi's death in 407 — ended with Gao Yun's brief reign; his assassination in 409 by Feng Ba inaugurated the successor Northern Yan.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution.
